title: Flux Keyboard
intro: Flux Keyboard 1.0.0: everything it adds over Pastiera 0.86, Pastiera's final feature release, then what the Pastiera team built between 0.85 and 0.86, which Flux Keyboard includes.

highlights.text: Flux Keyboard: its own name, app ID, icon (a keyboard, in Niagara's icon packs too) and home screen fitted to the Titan 2 Elite, crediting and linking the original Pastiera. The compact mode is called Solderina.

Layers as pages: the emoji layer and the symbols page open on your recents (topped up with their own, search on A, GIFs or the kaomoji on L), and Q and P turn through pages of every emoji by category and every symbol, going round at either end; the keys with a job keep it.

Shizuku extras (no root): the Titan 2's keyboard light on and off with the screen (never timing out while it's on), following the display's real brightness (adaptive brightness and fades included), or flashing for notifications, using the vendor calls PhysiBoard by brobata documented; screen size presets (Default at 300 dpi, Tablet and Desktop at a smallest width of 601 and 860 dp), also as shortcuts, a reset that puts back the density alone, and screen size per app, picked from a searchable list of apps (the density changes as each app comes to the front, and carries through the recent apps screen so it doesn't redraw mid-animation, while a home app of your own such as Niagara has its own size); and shortcuts to force-stop the app in front, toggle Battery Saver or cut the app in front off the network. Each screen size has its own Apply button, chosen apps show their icons, and Shizuku can be started at boot.
GIF search (KLIPY) in the picker and on the emoji layer, with favourites, recents and caching (a search's results are kept for a week after last use).

Kaomoji on the symbols page's P key: over 300 in Gboard's groups, a page of 24 at a time on taller keys, each key's letter under its kaomoji (P for the next page, Q for the one before), with the ones you typed last on a Recents page first. Pages stay open after a pick unless you choose otherwise (Close after picking).
Ctrl+Z undoes typing in any app, from the keyboard's own edit history; Ctrl+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y redoes it.
App shortcuts: the same shortcuts in every app, suggested per category, plus each app's own launcher shortcuts and settings (Ctrl+Alt+1–4, Ctrl+,).
Quick launcher: the built-in one by default, in the keyboard's theme colours, with apps' own long-press shortcuts ("New message", "Scan QR code") as results.

Trackpad swipes: optionally, swipe left, up or right anywhere on the trackpad for the left, middle or right suggestion, and choose whether a swipe left or down deletes the previous word. Short and slanted swipes count, whichever way they mostly go. Left and right swipes have their own sensitivity. While you type, the swipes go to the keyboard rather than scrolling the app underneath, and keyboard swipes per app (with Scroll assistant on for every app) chooses the apps they may scroll, or the ones they're kept from, with Select all.
Inline autofill: password manager chips (Bitwarden, say) in the suggestion bar, centred and drawn like its suggestion buttons in your theme's colours.

One-time codes: a code from a notification (sign-in, bank, delivery) is offered as a chip in the next text field for three minutes, and not again once typed. The code is the number next to a word like "code" or "PIN" (whole words: "shipping" and "security briefing" don't count), so order and account numbers aren't mistaken for it. Off until you give it notification access.

Recommended settings: the configuration Flux Keyboard is tuned with, from its own Titan 2 Elite, offered again after each update as a list of what would change (from your value to the recommended one, Apply all or Keep mine). A short list that suits nearly everyone (modifiers, suggestions, LEDs; on the Titan 2 Elite its trackpad swipes and compact bar), applied on a fresh install or with the Apply button in Privacy & system, which then offers to go through the rest. Matters of taste (auto-correct, GIFs, colours, what the emoji key opens) are switches on the tutorial's Your choices page, and settings that need a permission or another app (one-time codes, Niagara search, hidden-keyboard apps) start off and are set up from its Extras page.

A status bar fitted to the rounded display: straight LEDs and straight corner buttons by default, reaching down and out into the corners on every page (the bar, symbol and emoji pages), with filled corners, a 5 dp lift above the LEDs and room around the SYM screens. Or contoured LEDs, Pastiera's contour LEDs reworked: lit and unlit, they run round the display corners on two rails (Shift and Alt on the left; Shift or the emoji LED, Sym and Ctrl on the right) on every page at one height and the same length, drawn over everything, with the corner buttons following the same curve a small gap inside them. The display corners default to a shape calibrated on the phone, with smooth edges.

Background picture: your own picture behind the keys, dragged, zoomed and rotated into place on a preview of the bar. With Auto colours the keys are shaded against it with text that reads, and Key opacity sets how solid they are. It's kept in backups.

Clean copied links: a link you copy loses its tracking (utm_, fbclid, YouTube's si, is and ab_channel…) on the clipboard itself, so it's clean wherever it's pasted, and opens the full site rather than the mobile one. Google, AMP, Facebook, Instagram and YouTube redirects become the link they lead to, and pasting with Ctrl+V cleans too. Password managers' copies are left alone.

Spell checker: Flux Keyboard as Android's spell checker, underlining typos in any app, and reading words with apostrophes whole: contractions (couldn't, won't, can't) and elisions (l'homme, dell'anno).
Terminal mode: Termux gets the keyboard's Alt and SYM, a real Ctrl, a hidden keyboard and a choice of what the emoji key sends, including Alt.

improvements.text: Emoji picker key: a dedicated key (Right Shift by default), assigned by pressing it. A modifier key opens the picker when released, so it still works in chords like Ctrl+Shift+Q.

Hold or tap the emoji key: hold it and press a key to type that key's emoji from the emoji layer; optionally, one tap makes the next key do the same, a second tap opens the emoji screen, and Back cancels it. Held without choosing anything, it just lets go.

Tap SYM for one symbol (option): one tap makes the next key type its symbol without opening the symbols; a second tap opens them, and Back cancels it. Holding SYM works as before, and held without choosing anything it just lets go. (Modifiers & SYM > Tap, lock & long press.)
Symbol search across every Unicode symbol.
Skin tones: hold an emoji on the layer's pages for its skin tones, one per key, and choose a default skin tone for the picker and the layer.
Kaomoji search: ⌕ on the first kaomoji page searches them by mood, action, expression or name (lenny face, table flip, shrug).

Each picker search has its own tabs in the bottom bar: GIF search has favourites (★) and quick searches (LOL, Love, Sad, Wow, Yes, No, Bye), symbol search the symbols page's groups, and kaomoji search their moods (Joy, Love, Sad, Mad, Wow, Shy, Hug, Hi). Tapping one jumps straight to it; emoji search's category tabs clear the search and jump to the category.
Recent emoji first on the emoji layer (option): the ones you used last take its first keys and its own move along; the symbols page has Recents too.

Every panel (emoji, symbols, kaomoji, GIFs, clipboard) has corner buttons as wide as the bar's side buttons, reaching the display's sides, with its bottom keys centred between them; the GIF page's KLIPY credit has a line of its own above the GIFs.
Emoji layer: search, a Recents key, and profiles for common situations (chatting, work, social…) that can follow the app you're in.
Search, Recents and GIF keys on the layers have a tint of their own, and nothing in the default layers sits under them.
Emoji beyond the system font, and names for every emoji in search.

A search key (⌕) on every panel; letters type the layer's mappings unless type-to-search is on. What opens ready to type, the search key, what Enter picks and recently used first have a Search & Enter page of their own.
Learn words you use often: a word that isn't in the dictionary goes into it once you've typed it three times, so it's suggested and never auto-corrected (on by default).

Remember emails and phone numbers: ones you type yourself are kept in your dictionary and offered as chips in email and phone fields; tap one to fill the field. Nothing pasted or filled in, nothing from password fields (on by default).

Incognito typing: learn nothing when an app asks (private tabs), or always: no new words, emails or numbers, next-word predictions, word use, or recent emoji, symbols and GIFs. What was learned before is still offered. Words are never learned from password, email or web address fields.
Ctrl + Shift + D adds the last word you typed to the dictionary (Auto-correction > Dictionary, on by default), and the suggestions' “add to dictionary” chip can be switched off.

No automatic spaces after punctuation in email, sign-in, web address and password fields, nor inside numbers, times and decimals (1,000, 12:30, 3.14), and a clearer punctuation spacing dialog: each mark named, with No space before and Space after columns.

Emoticons keep their shape: punctuation typed straight into more, as in :-) ;( :D, gets no space after it; if a word follows (:Do) the space comes back. Double Space for a full stop is off by default.

Pick suggestions from the keyboard: Ctrl+Shift+Q, W or E takes the left, middle or right suggestion (Ctrl+1/2/3 on keyboards with a number row). Either Shift works, including Right Shift while it's the emoji key.
Shift + Backspace deletes forwards on the Titan too (the setting now sees a held Shift, and is among the recommended settings).
Select from the cursor: a key shortcut turns on Nav Mode with the selection anchored at the cursor, so arrows, Home, End and cursor swipes extend it.
Private mode: one key shortcut (or the quick launcher) turns on Incognito typing everywhere and Offline mode together.
Suggestion swipes learn from you: a pick you undo makes them need a little more, a swipe that falls short a little less.
Works with Gboard's spell checker: when Android's spell checker is another app's, its corrections join Flux Keyboard's suggestions.
Backspace undoes an auto-replace and keeps the space after it; text replacements can be undone with auto-replace off too.

Automatic Shift by field type: choose which kinds of text field start with a capital (text, names and addresses by default; search, links and email addresses off). A kind that's off gets no automatic Shift, even when an app asks for capitals. Fields that don't say what they are have an Other kind of their own (off until you choose it).

Paste suggestion: what you just copied, offered in the next text field (long text is shortened without breaking an emoji). In a password field it's offered as ⎘ •••••••• (never the text itself), including a password you copied from a password manager; those stay in memory only and never go into the clipboard history.
Emoji suggestions: an emoji for the word you're typing.

Exact typing (Apps): in the apps you pick (SSH clients, code editors, AI agents) nothing rewrites what you type: no auto-correct, text replacements, auto-capitals, double-space full stop or automatic spaces. Optionally also wherever an app itself asks for no suggestions.
Remember the language per app: each app gets back the language you last typed in there.
Snippets fill in {date}, {time}, {datetime}, {isodate}, {day} and {clipboard}.
Smart toggle: Alt and Ctrl switch themselves off by context.
Voice input keeps listening through pauses until you stop it or stay silent.
Ctrl+Shift+Space switches language backwards.
No automatic Shift in scripts without capitals (Thai, Arabic, CJK…).
Bold suggestions option.
Edit layouts in the app: tap a key to change what it types with and without Shift, then save, restore the original, save as a new layout or export it as JSON. No web editor needed.

Flux Keyboard's own quick launcher shortcuts for the apps in its app shortcut and Enter lists: New message, New post, New note or Compose email, and Search, each only where the app accepts it. They can be turned off on their own (Shortcuts for compatible apps).

Add a shortcut: put a shortcut an app offers for the home screen (a contact's direct dial, a bookmark, a settings page) in the quick launcher's results (Apps > Quick Launcher), or long-press an app in the quick launcher and pick Add a shortcut. Flux Keyboard also makes the common ones itself, for apps that only offer theirs to the home screen: call or message a contact (calling straight away if you allow the phone permission), a website, and Termux tasks (scripts in ~/.shortcuts, run as Termux:Widget runs them; needs allow-external-apps in Termux). Your Termux:Widget scripts and tasks are also listed in the quick launcher on their own, kept up to date (option).

Niagara search as the quick launcher (option): Back, the key or the gesture, before opening anything returns to the app you opened it from, and on Niagara's home screen the built-in quick launcher opens instead.
Search bars wait for typing (option): when an app opens with its search bar focused, the keyboard bar stays hidden until you type or tap the bar (also palsoftware/pastiera#319).

Termux set up in one paste: a command, copied for you with Termux opened (in the tutorial and Terminal mode), lets other apps run commands (the quick launcher's scripts need it) and removes the extra-keys row and its text box, which a phone with keys doesn't need.

Pastiera's Enter per app gets standards by app category: chat apps send with Enter (Shift + Enter for a new line), email and note apps keep Enter for new lines and send with Ctrl + Enter, and every installed chat, email and notes app is listed to change. Search boxes and one-line fields always get their own action (search, go, next).
Terminal apps get no microphone button.

Hidden-keyboard apps (Niagara Launcher and Termux:X11 by default; others from the tutorial), with LEDs and panels per app; only the LEDs that are lit show there, where the LEDs usually are. Niagara keeps its LEDs and the emoji and symbols panels by default, for quick replies from notifications. The keyboard bar no longer pops up on Niagara's home screen (palsoftware/pastiera#319). SYM chords reach the keyboard there, so SYM + Space opens the quick launcher instead of the symbols panel.
The quick launcher opens from other apps (key mappers, Tasker) and the app icon.
Linux desktop keyboard layout from the keyboard's Alt map and SYM page.

Trackpad swipes on the Titan 2 Elite: they reach the keyboard only while the phone's Scroll assistant is on (Settings > Gestures > Keyboard gesture), which the trackpad tutorial and the phone trackpad settings row explain; Cursor assistant is optional, but its cursor mode takes the swipes. A suggestion swipe needs only about one key's width (a tenth of the trackpad), so sliding from one key onto the next picks, however slowly within half a second.
The phone trackpad settings row opens the phone's Scroll assistant page directly.

Every Titan 2 Elite setting on one screen, and a phone trackpad settings shortcut (also a quick launcher command) that opens the phone's Keyboard gesture page directly (Unihertz's own settings app, com.agui.settings), or Settings search with it ready to paste on other phones.

Per-LED colours, a clear active-to-locked jump and an optional sweeping gradient when locked, set from one table with Off, Active and Locked columns. Shift is blue, Ctrl orange, Alt green, SYM purple and the emoji key pink by default.

SYM's LED is lit while SYM is held and locked while it's tapped for one symbol or the symbols are open. A fifth LED does the same for the emoji key (on by default; Look & sound > Status LED colours); all five LEDs share the width equally.
Wallpaper colours (option): the keyboard takes its colours from your wallpaper.

The keyboard follows the system's dark and light mode with Pastiera's Classic Midnight and Classic Cloud themes. The Keyboard theme page chooses the theme on the page itself, explains which theme is used when, and marks the one in use.
A customisable menu bar (which buttons, in what order) with a GIF button, and a preview of it at its real height.

A tutorial of its own: one-step setup, every new feature, Your choices (auto-correct, double-space full stop, emoji suggestions, GIF search, what the emoji key opens, wallpaper colours, each a switch), a page for making it yours, and the extras that need a permission, on pages that scroll. The trackpad has its own up-to-date guide. After an update, What's new shows alone, lists only what's new since the version you had (nothing at all after an update with nothing new), and closes with ✕ or Done.

Updates from this fork: Flux Keyboard checks this repository's releases, not upstream's, compares versions properly, and downloads and installs the update itself (Android asks before installing). Choose full releases only (always the latest, however many dev builds follow it), or dev builds too; a dev build starts on dev updates and a full release on releases. Dev builds are offered with their build time ("1.0.1 dev · 6 Oct 2026, 11:50").

Restricted settings: features that need the accessibility service or notification access say when Android blocks them for apps installed from a file, explain step by step how to allow them (in settings and the tutorial), and open App info to lift the block. The tutorial's extras page always shows the steps.
Setting links: hold a setting for a fluxkeyboard://setting/… link that opens it in this app, and release notes link to this changelog; nothing points at Pastiera's website.
Backups include every setting, the background picture and the display corner calibration.

Settings grouped by task, ordered by usefulness, related switches merged into tables (closing after a pick, search, layer pages, Shift/Alt/Ctrl behaviour, capitals, learning), searchable, with rows sized to their text, and choices that go together in one dropdown (which swipe deletes a word). Search keeps your query and your place when you open a result and come back, and nothing is focused on its own.
Input Languages laid out like every other page.
Offline mode: nothing in the keyboard goes online.
Settings for hardware the phone doesn't have (Clicks keyboard, Titan 2 layout) stay hidden.
A debug export (Copy or Share) with the last fields opened, password manager suggestions and Automatic Shift's decisions, text masked.
Developer options gather the Dev builds update switch and calibration and debug tools; they're on by default in dev builds and off in full releases.
Shift, Alt and Ctrl side by side (Modifiers & SYM): what a tap does, whether two taps lock it, what Space does, whether it lets go after use, and whether Backspace with it deletes forwards.
Pills for switches that belong together: Learn as you type (words, emails and numbers), Capital after (a full stop, an emoticon) and Show as pages (emoji layer, symbols).
Defaults: suggestion swipes at 100, Ctrl+Space as the only layout switch, and pages that stay open after a pick.
Text replacement examples in your language ("dont → don't" in English).
Device SYM layer editor with curated and custom profiles.
The pencil on the symbol panels edits that layer's mapping; holding it on pages that have them edits the variations.
Dev's choice static variations by default.

Keyboard swipes per app can include Flux Keyboard itself, so swiping on the keyboard doesn't scroll its own settings; the swipes still reach the keyboard while you type there. The quick launcher keeps the choice of the app it opens over.
About ends with the flux sniffer mods mark, light or dark to match the app's theme (tap it for their GitHub), and has a Support me on Ko-fi link.

A much smaller app: English comes built in, and other languages' dictionaries download the first time you use them (or from Installed dictionaries), from Flux Keyboard's own releases. Languages you already type in download by themselves after the update.
Minimal mode (Look & sound): no keyboard bar in any app, the LEDs optional, while the keys work as usual and the emoji and symbols pages still open on their keys.

Keyboard swipes through Shizuku: with Shizuku running, swipes on the keys reach the keyboard in every app, whether or not the phone's Scroll assistant scrolls it, so Scroll assistant can be switched off for the apps you want kept still. It's the default for Shizuku users until you pick a source.

Extra keys: Esc, Tab, Ctrl, Alt and arrows in the bar's place, Termux style, from the menu bar, a shortcut or the emoji key in terminal apps (its new default there). While the row is open, Q to P press its keys, and its Ctrl or Alt goes with the next key you press. Text fields get their own set: arrows, Home, End, select all, cut, copy and paste.
Terminals: Nav Mode works in Termux, sending its arrows straight to the terminal, and swipes on the keys move the cursor (Terminal mode > Swipes move the cursor).
The keyboard bar is Solderina, with Minimal mode beside it (Look & sound > Keyboard bar); the older extended bar is retired. The minimal mode shortcut and menu button switch it on the spot.
The menu bar starts with extra keys, undo, redo, the clipboard and settings, with its first and last buttons the same size as the bar's corner buttons, so the LEDs stay clear.

Shizuku at boot through Termux:Boot: the Termux setup command offers to start Shizuku by itself after a restart, waiting for Wi-Fi, pairing Termux with wireless debugging once and finding Shizuku wherever it's installed.

A new tutorial start: allowing restricted settings goes try, allow, try again and ends with the accessibility service on; a page to pick Solderina or minimal mode; and a Shizuku page from download to starting after a restart, with links to Shizuku, Termux and Termux:Boot on GitHub.
Language versions: full releases come as one APK per language, each opening in its translation and its language's usual layout, and updating to the same language's APK.
In minimal mode the LEDs sit right on the screen's edge.

Built-in shell (Shell access): pair once with wireless debugging, typing the code into Flux Keyboard's notification, and Flux Keyboard runs its own developer shell, with no Shizuku or Termux needed. After a restart it starts by itself once Wi-Fi connects, switching wireless debugging on just for that. Shizuku still works when the built-in shell isn't set up.
The keyboard light fades smoothly with the screen: the screen's brightness is read 30 times a second, and once a frame while it's changing.
Clean links covers shops and more sites: Etsy, eBay and Amazon worldwide, AliExpress, Temu, Walmart, Target, Booking, Airbnb, Google search and others.
After a picked suggestion, punctuation goes straight next to the word, and Enter drops the space.
Swipe down to delete a word buzzes like the suggestion swipes (Trackpad settings, on by default).
While Shizuku isn't running yet (no Wi-Fi after a restart), Android's own trackpad swipes stand in until it is (Trackpad settings, on by default).
The currency key knows more currencies, and each language version uses its own when the phone's region doesn't say.

Emoji, symbols and kaomoji open on a default page, Developer's pick of the most used until you change it: the pencil in the bottom-left corner (where the emoji and symbols switch was) maps it, and your recents are one page back on Q. To open on your recents instead, tick them in Start on recents (Emoji layer settings).

Gaming mode (Shell access > Gaming mode): in apps with a game profile, keys reach the game as they are, mapped once in the emulator's or launcher's own controller settings, and the trackpad plays its sticks: GameNative's and GameHub's on-screen sticks, or the direction keys an emulator maps like any other key.

Gaming mode: the games found in the game folders and the games with a profile are in the quick launcher too, started as their home screen shortcuts start them (Games in the quick launcher, in Gaming mode).

Gaming mode: Stream to Moonlight (first step): the phone shows up in Moonlight on your TV or another device on the same Wi-Fi, pairs with the PIN Moonlight shows, and lists your games there with their art. Cloud games are left out, played on the TV straight from the cloud. Streaming a game itself comes next.

Gaming mode: Xbox Cloud Gaming plays in Flux Keyboard's own player (xbox.com/play), where the keys and trackpad are a controller in Flux Keyboard's layout, for every cloud game. Add an Xbox cloud game adds it, or any game Xbox Cloud Gaming streams (from Microsoft's catalogue), each with its box art and its own settings, started straight into the game. Sign in to Xbox opens Xbox's sign-in with the keys typing, and keys type into any text field in the player. The Games app can add games too.

Gaming mode: an app that looks like a game, with no settings yet, gets a notification offering to set it up. Xbox Cloud Gaming is recognised. A Play Store page or sign-in opened inside a game keeps its screen, the screen switches faster, and swiping a game away in recents ends gaming mode. A stick stroke starting near the trackpad's edge still reaches full push. With root, Volume Up and Down are the left shoulder and trigger and the red side key the right trigger. The quick launcher starts games the way the Games app does.

Gaming mode: games found in the game folders, and games installed from the Play Store, join the games list by themselves, not set up (and not played with) until you say: the first time one starts, it asks to set it up or play it with its app's settings. The Games app has each game's settings too (⚙).

Gaming mode: Games in the app list adds a Games app to the home screen's app list (Niagara's too) with every game, and every game can be added to the home screen at once. Screen is now as the app wants or kept upright (forcing a landscape resolution, the default for game apps). A Dolphin Wii game can take a GameCube controller (Mario Kart Wii), the Wii pointer follows the trackpad's right half, GameCube L and R sit on the volume keys, games named by their file get their title, and keys pressed while steering no longer stop the left stick. Record the trackpad moved to Developer options.

Gaming mode: one controller layout everywhere: W A S D the d-pad, O K P L the face buttons where a controller has them, Q E the shoulders, Z C the triggers, Space Start, Enter Select, Backspace Home, F and H the stick presses, J B N M the right stick and the trackpad's left half the left stick. The real controller (root) plays it, and Set up Dolphin's (or PPSSPP's) controls writes it into the emulator's own controller settings. A Dolphin Wii game can be given a Classic Controller or a Wii Remote held sideways instead of the Nunchuk (Wii controller, in the game's settings).

Gaming mode: the trackpad follows one finger at a time, so moving to the other half holds the first stick where it was until you lift. Right stick on keys puts the right stick on J B N M, with the trackpad's left half the left stick, so both move together. Record the trackpad (in Gaming mode) saves what the trackpad reports, to share.

Gaming mode: for games with only touch controls, Place keys on screen (gaming mode's notification) puts a key on each of the game's buttons: holding the key holds the button. Sticks are placed the same way.
Layer editor: start the default page from your recents, or with the most popular.
Battery Saver and the brightness keys work without the shell too.

Gaming mode: Add a game from a game launcher also finds GameNative's and GameHub's installed Steam games, and each profile can go on the home screen: its shortcut switches the profile on and starts the game (GameNative's straight away).

Gaming mode: Sideways-only game, for apps like GameHub that turn the screen whatever they're told: while it runs, the screen is made landscape-shaped instead, so the phone stays upright. For GameNative, its own Portrait mode per game does the job.
Layer pages: an arrow leading to a recents page shows the recents icon, and symbols Alt already types come after the others.
Terminal mode: the emoji key held as Alt is the terminal's own Alt (Meta, Esc first in Termux), not the keyboard's Alt characters.
Termux setup only sets Termux up again; starting Shizuku at boot through Termux is its own command, offered on the Shizuku route.

Gaming mode: Make the game folders sets up Download/Flux Keyboard/Games with a folder for GameNative, GameHub, Dolphin, PPSSPP, Azahar and Eden. GameNative's and GameHub Lite's Export for frontend files and emulator games there (and in ES-DE's ROMs folder) each get a profile and a home screen shortcut that starts straight into the game.
Gaming mode: add game folders of your own, the same ones set in a launcher or emulator, each read for one emulator's or launcher's games or by its folders' names.

Gaming mode: add a game yourself, like GameNative's and GameHub's custom games: pick the launcher or emulator you added it to, then its file, exported file or game ID, and it gets a profile and a home screen shortcut that starts it.
Gaming mode: one Screen choice per game (as the app wants, kept upright, or a sideways game with the phone upright), switched along with the game; the sideways screen sits clear of the camera cutout.
Gaming mode: keys mapped on a drawing of the keyboard (tap a key and pick its action) or of a controller (tap a button and press its key).
Gaming mode: a launcher's game player is covered by the launcher's profile, and an app a game ran in without a profile is offered to add to one.
Number fields take a decimal point, minus and the like from their keys, in the separator the phone uses.
Gaming mode: Dolphin and PPSSPP get graphics settings suited to the phone's GPU (Vulkan and the right options for the Titan 2 Elite's Mali), with advice for games whose settings can't be written.
Gaming mode: the phone's own game mode (com.agui.game) is one switch, no pop-up.
Gaming mode: each game can have its own resolution, on the phone and when streaming (Infinity Nikki at 720p, say), keeping the shape its Screen choice gives it.
Gaming mode: Reset puts an emulator's controller and graphics settings back to how they were before Flux Keyboard set them.
Gaming mode: the trackpad's left stick works in Dolphin without setting it up by hand: it presses keys the keyboard has (R T Y G), which Dolphin's profile maps to the stick.
Gaming mode: on-screen keys are placed separately for the phone and for streaming, the placer opens from the streaming notification, and keys are picked from a grid as well as pressed.
Gaming mode: pick a game's art from everything its sources have, upright and icon, or a picture of your own.

Games app: a grid of upright covers with names, Add a game and Xbox cloud game among them, launchers and emulators on a page of their own, settings behind the gear and streaming on the chip at the top. Long-press a game for its settings.
Xbox Cloud Gaming: the sign-in page closes by itself once you're signed in, and long-pressing the Xbox tile signs you out (it asks first).
Stream to Moonlight: Automatic runs at exactly the resolution the Moonlight client asks for (4K included); 720p, 1080p or 1440p run the game smaller, scaled up on the client.
Stream to Moonlight: the phone asks before a Moonlight client starts a stream (Don't ask again per device), and a notification shows what's streaming where, with End stream and Place keys.
Stream to Moonlight: Moonlight shows each game's upright art (the art you picked), the phone's own screen can be listed as well, and Xbox cloud games are listed once played in Flux Keyboard's player.

Stream to Moonlight: a game can play on a screen of its own instead of the phone's being mirrored, leaving the phone free. The Games app shows that screen live, and your keys, touch, placed keys and trackpad sticks go to it. Android 16's desktop can be shown there too. The notification switches either way mid-stream.
Stream to Moonlight: on a screen of its own, keyboards, mice and controllers plugged into the phone or paired by Bluetooth go straight to the game, and back to the phone after.
Stream to Moonlight works over USB tethering and Ethernet as well as Wi-Fi: Moonlight is given the address it reached the phone by.

Games app: launchers and emulators get upright tiles like the games, the Xbox cloud tile shows Game Pass art, and games from the Play Store stay on the games page instead of also being listed as launchers.
Xbox Cloud Gaming: hold Space for the Xbox button; a tap is still Start.
Xbox Cloud Gaming: a game opened from the Games app goes back there when you quit it, instead of leaving you in Xbox's library.
Clearer wording throughout gaming and streaming settings, such as Choose artwork from the internet in place of Found art.
Games app: launchers and emulators show their SteamGridDB artwork (Dolphin, PPSSPP, GameHub and others), falling back to their icon.

Games app: move through it with the same keys as in games (W A S D to move, L to open, K for a game's settings, P to go back, Q or E to switch pages, Space for gaming settings) or a controller. On by default, in Gaming settings.
Games app: long-press Stream for streaming settings (mirror or separate screen, resolution, devices, paired clients); a tap still turns it on or off.
Stream to Moonlight: Moonlight's Wake starts streaming on the phone when it's off, so a game can be picked straight away.
Stream to Moonlight: every XCloud game in the games list is listed in Moonlight, played yet or not.
Stream to Moonlight: notifications show as usual while streaming (Android 15 and later hide them during screen capture; put back after).
Stream to Moonlight: the phone's screen has its own cover in Moonlight, Mirror phone screen on a dark gradient.
Games app: pick artwork for launchers, emulators and the XCloud tile, which is now called XCloud Games and skips covers with a white frame.
Games app: keys picked with W A S D now show a frame round the tile, with the rest dimmed.
XCloud Games in the Games app: tap a game to play it straight away; long-press it to add it to the Games app and Moonlight without playing, or open its settings.

Games app: emulators and launchers are looked up on SteamGridDB under the names it lists them by (Dolphin Emulator, Citra for Azahar, Yuzu for Eden, PCSX2 for AetherSX2 and more), so most get artwork automatically.

Stream to Moonlight: XCloud Games (Xbox Cloud Gaming's library, with its tile's art) and Android desktop (the phone's desktop on a screen of its own, the phone left free) are listed in Moonlight beside the phone's screen.
Stream to Moonlight: Android desktop switches Developer options' desktop windowing on by itself (a restart may be needed the first time; the phone says so).
Choosing artwork from the internet has a search box: look up any title for a game, launcher or emulator without renaming it.

Game screen page: choose where input goes. Touch works on the screen as you touch it, or as a trackpad (one finger moves a pointer, tap to click, two-finger tap to right-click, two fingers to scroll); keys go to the screen or stay with the phone. Android desktop starts as a trackpad.
Stream to Moonlight: the phone screen and Android desktop covers read Mirror Phone Screen and Android Desktop.
Stream to Moonlight: Flux Games opens the Games app on the TV, zoomed out to a TV's layout with the controller frame showing; Flux Games, Android Desktop and Mirror Phone Screen are listed first.
Games app: it opens from Moonlight whether or not Games in the app list is on.
Xbox Cloud Gaming's own entry (in the XCloud catalogue, the Games app and Moonlight) shows the XCloud Games tile's art.
XCloud Games: a game you open and play is added to the Games app and Moonlight by itself; long-press it in the catalogue to remove it.
Games app: the gear sits on the right beside Stream, a long title scrolls sideways, and streaming's settings open as a page of their own.
Quick launcher: Flux Games, XCloud Games and streaming's settings are commands of their own, and XCloud games show as XCloud Games.

Gaming mode: placed sticks can be resized in the placer, each with a dead zone and a range; a push is a circle (a diagonal no further than straight), the circle's edge is a full push, and touches stay on the screen, so pushing down works on a sideways screen too.
Gaming mode: Back in a game asks to be pressed again before leaving, so a stray press doesn't quit.
Gaming mode: the screen's density follows a sideways or lower resolution, so a game's screen holds as much as the phone's own (put back after).

Gaming mode: in games played by touch (Play Store games, or any with keys placed on their screen), the trackpad moves the game's own on-screen sticks from the start, placed where most touch games draw them; move or resize them in the placer.
XCloud Games: choose your Game Pass plan (Ultimate, Premium or Essential) and the catalogue lists only the cloud games it includes, from Microsoft's own Game Pass lists.
Gaming mode: hold SYM and press Volume Up or Down to change the volume, even in games that use the volume keys as buttons

Gaming mode: Dolphin's on-screen controls are set up for the trackpad when a game starts: the stick centres where it's touched, and the controls are invisible (they still work). Settings you've changed yourself in Dolphin are kept

Gaming mode: new keyboard controls that work like a controller: W A Z D the left stick (SYM for the d-pad, right Shift for the right stick), I J M L the face buttons (Alt for the right stick), S and K the stick clicks, Q and E the bumpers, the volume keys the triggers, Space Start (Shift for Select, Alt for Xbox/Home). See Gaming settings > Keyboard controls

Gaming mode: the trackpad no longer plays the sticks by default (the Wii pointer stays). Gaming settings now explain what the keyboard can and can't do, and recommend a phone controller for the best experience
Gaming mode: the root-only controller mode is gone; the keyboard controls work without root

Streaming: lower latency: the phone's Wi-Fi is kept out of power saving while streaming, the stream is marked as real-time traffic for routers that honour it, and the video encoder never waits on later frames
Crash log: a Clear logs option empties the logs so the next crash log saves quickly and holds only what happened since

Streaming: Always available to Moonlight keeps the phone listed while streaming is off, for Moonlight apps whose Wake can't reach the phone (like the one for LG TVs); picking a game turns streaming on
Gaming mode: Keyboard controls shows the keyboard with the button each key is, alone or with SYM, Shift, right Shift or Alt held; tap a key to change it
Gaming mode: for a GameCube controller in Dolphin, the volume keys press L and R all the way with their click; Alt + Volume presses them all the way without it

Gaming mode: more emulators recognised (RetroArch, Lemuroid, DuckStation, NetherSX2, melonDS, DraStic, NooDS, Panda3DS, Mupen64Plus, Flycast and others), so their games start the right way up; keys are bound in their own settings
Gaming mode: Keep the game upright, a screen choice for DS and 3DS emulators (their two screens one above the other), the default for them

Gaming mode: Bottom screen (touch), a trackpad choice that touches a DS or 3DS's bottom screen like a stylus; both halves set to it use the whole trackpad, and the area can be moved and sized in Place keys on screen
Gaming mode: Swap A/B and X/Y, on by default for Nintendo emulators (Dolphin, Eden, Azahar, melonDS and others), so each key presses the button in its place

Gaming mode: keys handled one way per game. Dolphin reads the keyboard itself, so it gets every key untouched and the whole layout lives in its controls. Every other game has each of the layout's keys taken and the one key for its control sent, or a controller's buttons and sticks for a game that takes a controller. Keys outside the layout always reach the game as they are

Lighter and quicker: settings read once instead of on every key, nothing made afresh each time the keyboard's bars and pointer are drawn, number settings kept without extra objects, settings saved in the background, unused code taken out
A smaller app: unused text, colours and icon images taken out, in every language

Typing and trackpad swipes do less work per key: your own corrections are read once until you change them, accents and swipe readings no longer rebuild their patterns each time, and the emoji layer opens straight away the first time
Gaming mode: the volume keys are the triggers as the phone sits held sideways, Volume Down the left and Volume Up the right

Dolphin: each game can have its own keys for its controller, set on a drawing of the GameCube controller, Wii Remote and Nunchuk, Classic Controller or sideways Wii Remote, including shaking and tilting the Wii Remote (a wheelie button in Mario Kart Wii, say). Kept as a Dolphin profile for that game

Gaming mode: any game or app can have keys of its own, on top of Keyboard controls, changed on the keyboard drawing in its settings. They work in every emulator and launcher gaming mode sends buttons to (PPSSPP, RetroArch, GameHub and others)
Gaming mode: the keys page shows the keyboard or a controller. On the controller, each button shows the keys that press it; tap one to give it a key
Gaming mode: the controller drawings show just the buttons where they sit, without the controller's outline
Gaming mode: give a controller button its key by pressing the key itself (with a modifier held if you like), on the controller drawings and Dolphin's

Dolphin: a game started from Games plays with its own controller and keys straight away, with nothing to load in Dolphin's game settings, and each game can hide Dolphin's on-screen controls, keep them invisible for sticks and keys placed on them, or show them
Dolphin: each game uses Flux Keyboard's controls even if a profile was chosen for it in Dolphin; a switch in the game's settings keeps Dolphin's own profile instead
Gaming mode: with the official GameHub installed, a note recommends GameHub Lite, which starts each game straight away; the official app's games now just open it
Gaming mode: the screen choices are now called Landscape and Portrait; game apps stay on Landscape, DS and 3DS emulators on Portrait

Gaming mode: a Screens choice for DS and 3DS games: both screens either way up, one big and one small, side by side, or one alone, written into Azahar (and the Citra builds) as the game starts, and into NooDS for all its games; Screen follows it, and so does the trackpad's bottom-screen area. melonDS, DraStic, Panda3DS and Cemu keep theirs private, so a note says where to set them
Gaming mode: the controller remappers show the keys on a button, each taken off with a tap, and Keyboard controls' button picker has No key

Stream to Moonlight: with root on in Shell access, the Wake an LG TV's Moonlight sends (to port 9, which no app can open) is passed on to Flux Keyboard; without root, Always available keeps the phone listed instead
Games app: Stream is a broadcast mark whose arcs show the phone's Wi-Fi strength while streaming is on (dimmed while it's off); tap to turn it on or off, long-press for its settings

Stream to Moonlight: Phone's sound while streaming: the game's sound off on the phone (the default; the Moonlight client still gets it), or every sound of the phone's off too (calls and messages vibrate, alarms still sound), all put back when the stream ends

Stream to Moonlight: a Moonlight client can be set up (LG webOS for now: found on the Wi-Fi, accepted once on it); with streaming on, picking a game in the Games app turns it on and opens Moonlight there straight into the game

Game folders: GameHub Lite has a folder of its own (Download/Flux Keyboard/Games/GameHub Lite) for its Steam library, apart from GameHub's; games already found in GameHub's folder still start in GameHub Lite when it's installed
Crash logs show where games are found: the game folders, Steam libraries and launcher shortcuts, and how each game was matched to its app

GameHub Lite with the official GameHub: Lite has no Export for frontend, so install both and export from the official GameHub; its games start in GameHub Lite, or in GameHub if you choose (Gaming mode > GameHub's games start in). Games already found move with the choice

Stream to Moonlight: with a Moonlight client set up and streaming on, opening a game (from the Games app, the home screen or the quick launcher) asks whether to stream it to the Moonlight client or play it on the phone; Games opened while streaming can be set to always one instead
Stream to Moonlight: the TV settings and prompts now say Moonlight client

README, changelog and settings text brought up to date: streaming described as it works now, the official GameHub's Export for frontend explained where the game folders are made, and GameHub Lite named among the launchers
Keyboard swipes' and the keyboard light's notes say Shell access rather than Shizuku, and Install Shizuku only shows when the built-in shell isn't set up
The app is now Flux Hub: its icon and settings are called Flux Hub, while the keyboard keeps the name Flux Keyboard in Android's keyboard list. Updates now come from the Flux-Hub repository

upstream.text: Clicks Power Keyboard support: controls, firmware status, and SYM profiles for Razr and Pixel.
An on-screen keyboard mode based on AOSP, with themes, a number row, layout styles and long-press layers.
Keyboard themes with an editor, draft themes, per-app theme assignment and transparent presets.
Titan 2 Elite geometry: rounded corners on the keyboard and status bar, calibrated contours and a gapless mode.
Settings overhaul, with search and shareable deep links.
Learned next-word suggestions, bigrams, suggestions from several dictionaries, and adding words from substitutions and swipes.
Snippet expansion, and emoji and symbol shortcodes.
Punctuation spacing (French spacing, closing brackets, commas), smart punctuation and mid-word quote replacement.
Native trackpad gestures on the Titan 2 and Titan 2 Elite, with separate sensitivities.
Original Titan keyboard profile and Alt keymap.
A unified QuickLauncher with Niagara search, and Home and document navigation actions.
Configurable modifier latching and indicators, Alt+Enter layout switching, Shift for Nav Mode, bounce keys and tap haptics.
Greek translation, and configurable status buttons for the compact mode (Pastierina, called Solderina here).
Clipboard history hidden while the phone is locked.
Safer backups (themes and typing sounds included) and many fixes: suggestions in Telegram, emoji search, Firefox accents, Ctrl shortcuts in number fields and more.

Contour LEDs on the Titan 2 Elite and Display contour calibration, which Flux Keyboard reworks into its optional contoured LEDs (see above); straight buttons are Flux Keyboard's default. Pastiera's "Fill lower display corners" is Flux Keyboard's Fill corners setting.
The menu bar shows SYM while it is held, and the navigation bar under the keyboard takes the keyboard's colour.
A software bill of materials (CycloneDX) in release builds, exported from About.

bugFixes.text: Deleting every custom input style now removes them from Android's language switcher too; before, the last ones could stay listed.
One-time codes are found in conversation notifications (texts and chats) on Android 10 as well.
The Clicks Power Keyboard's charging automation keeps following its settings; before, it could stop noticing changes after a while.
Ctrl+Z undo works only on fields it can read whole, so it never changes the wrong place, and redo keeps its step when the field can't be read.
Double space types a full stop only after something you typed, not at the start of a field or line.
Automatic Shift no longer capitalises in the middle of a long field that the app hands over in part.
Cursor and selection keys (Shift with the arrows, word by word) move to the right place in long fields.
Links to web pages no longer crash the app on a phone without a browser.
An imported dictionary is saved exactly as checked, never half-written when copying fails.
Minimal mode no longer leaves a coloured strip at the bottom of apps: with only the LEDs showing, the app keeps the whole screen.
Reinstalling starts fresh, tutorial included: Android no longer brings back an old copy of the settings from its cloud backup (the in-app backup, and moving to a new phone, still carry them).
Allowing Flux Keyboard in Shizuku always says what's happening: when Shizuku isn't running, remembers a refusal or doesn't show its question, Flux Keyboard says where to allow it and opens Shizuku.
The menu bar keeps its shape with more buttons than it started with.
Cursor swipes in terminals need a longer move before the cursor goes, so it no longer jumps at a touch.
A password manager's chip answers a tap anywhere on it, not just on its middle.
The built-in shell keeps running when Wi-Fi drops or wireless debugging goes off, and starts again by itself if it stops.
Screen size per app no longer flickers when another app's floating window (a widget, a picker) opens over an app with its own size.
A full stop, comma, ! or ? straight after a picked suggestion goes next to the word, whichever way it's typed (Alt, a long press or the key itself).
An email or phone number chip no longer stays on the bar in other apps once you've left its field.
A password manager's chips sit in the middle of the bar.
With Alt on, a layer's arrows, search and GIF or kaomoji keys keep their jobs instead of typing their labels.
Kaomoji in the kaomoji editor shrink to fit their keys.
The shortcut sheet follows the keyboard's theme, its labels on two lines instead of scrolling.
Bar buttons settings: the extra keys headings are readable, and the header stays below the status bar.
Shell access no longer talks about Shizuku where the built-in shell does the job.
In terminals, the emoji key's LED lights while it's held or its extra keys row is open, whatever it's set to.
Gaming mode follows the app in front the same way screen size per app does, so widgets, floating windows and recents no longer flip the screen.
Add a game from a game launcher finds games installed on shared storage (GameNative's own folder, Steam libraries).

A game's home screen shortcut opens that game: emulators start afresh with it (Dolphin and PPSSPP otherwise kept what was open), games from Export for frontend files use their exact store, and an app that can't be told the game is opened instead of nothing happening.
An email address or link picked from the suggestions gets its space only once a word follows, so sign-in fields don't reject it.

One-time codes: offered only in fields a code goes in and gone on leaving the field, typed box by box as each box takes its digit, and read again on Android 15, which hides them from notification readers.
Gaming mode: a game exported twice for frontends is listed once, GameHub's exported games are found, and game covers stay out of the gallery.
Gaming mode: a GameNative game no longer starts upside down, and a profile picked from the notification stays until another game starts.
What's new and release notes take each entry's time from the commit that added it, so they no longer skip or repeat changes.
Gaming mode: GameHub's Steam games are listed by name.
Shell access has its own row on the main settings page, with links to every setting elsewhere that uses it.
Gaming mode names emulator games by what they are, not their file: Wii, GameCube and 3DS games by their game ID in GameTDB's lists, PSP games by the title they carry.

Gaming mode's profiles show their game's art: Steam games' from Steam (GameNative and GameHub), Wii, GameCube and 3DS covers from GameTDB, and other emulator games' box art from libretro's thumbnails.
Gaming mode puts the screen's size and turning back as soon as another app is in front, even when it stopped without undoing them.

Use root (Shell access): on a rooted phone, shell commands run through su, ready at boot without pairing or Wi-Fi. With it, gaming mode can play as a real controller the game sees as plugged in, and the keyboard light can dim in its LEDs' own fine steps.

Gaming mode's settings are per app: a launcher's or emulator's games all play with them (Dolphin has one for GameCube games and one for Wii games, picked by each game's file), and a game only needs its own when its sticks sit elsewhere.
Suggestions read as they'll be typed: I, I'm, names and places with their capitals, a capital first letter with Shift on or after a typed capital, and all capitals with Caps Lock.
Xbox Cloud Gaming no longer freezes after typing an email address or on opening: the keyboard waited on the page, which waited on the keyboard. A crashed page reloads the player only.
The crash log includes why the app last closed and any not-responding traces, so freezes can be found too.
The Games app's top bar sits below the status bar and the camera cutout.
A game picked in Moonlight opens once the phone's screen has changed size, so GameHub opens the game rather than its library.
Moonlight's Wake starts streaming even when Android won't start the streaming service from the background, and each wake packet is noted in the crash log.

Moonlight's list no longer flickers coming back from a stream: entries stay the same, covers are sent the same each time (a game without one gets its name on the dark gradient), and a cover only changes when you pick new cover art for it.
A game on a separate screen fills it, even with Developer options' Enable freeform windows on secondary display on (Android desktop still opens as a desktop).
If Flux Keyboard closes mid-stream (a crash), the phone's screen size and turning, its notification setting and its desktop setting go back to normal as soon as it starts again.
Typing in the Games app (renaming a game, searching) works again: its controller keys only move through the grid.
After leaving a stream in Moonlight, another one starts straight away, without turning streaming off and on.
Games opened from Moonlight (on a separate screen or mirrored) open by themselves, even with Flux Keyboard in the background.
Keyboard swipes' settings say Shell access, which they use, not Shizuku; artwork settings say covers show in the Games app as well as Moonlight.
Placed keys tap in touch-only games again: their touches were numbered beyond what Android accepts (0 to 31), so it dropped them. The Game screen page's touches had the same fault.
Gaming mode: a trackpad stick pushes all the way down, measured from where your finger can actually reach on the keyboard
Crash log: includes Flux Keyboard's own record of gaming mode, streaming and game launches, kept even after the phone's log has moved on
XCloud Games: games with an apostrophe or accent in their name (like Crash Bandicoot 4: It's About Time) start again, and the player no longer returns to Games while a game is still loading
XCloud Games: a game that opens on its own page first (like Crash Bandicoot 4) is started with its Play button for you

Gaming mode: an on-screen stick near the edge of a game drawn smaller than the screen (Dolphin and other emulators, or while streaming) is pushed into the black bars around it, as a finger would, so it reaches all the way
Gaming mode: the volume keys work as triggers in Dolphin and PPSSPP
Gaming mode: Back works normally in an emulator's file browser, menus and other apps; only the game itself asks you to press Back twice

Gaming mode: pressing a button while using a trackpad stick no longer stops or recentres the stick: it stays where it was pushed while the button is held, then follows your thumb again from where it first landed
Gaming mode: if its key sender stops (as it could while streaming), it starts again by itself, and keys reach the game as they are meanwhile instead of being lost
Streaming: a controller on the Moonlight device now works in Dolphin, PPSSPP and the Xbox player, pressed as the keys their controls were given
Updates: tapping the update notification downloads and installs the update, as the update dialog does, instead of opening the release page
Gaming mode: Dolphin and PPSSPP set up with Flux Keyboard's older layout get the new one by themselves the next time a game starts from Games
Gaming mode: Flux Keyboard's own Xbox player gets the keyboard controls too (the volume keys as triggers)
Gaming mode: leaving a game and coming back no longer leaves keys or SYM counted as held (which turned the volume keys into volume, or ignored a button's next press)
Gaming mode: a Dolphin Wii game set to a GameCube controller gets it again each time it starts from Games

Gaming mode: in Dolphin, PPSSPP and the Xbox player, a key that is its own button goes to the game as it is; only combinations (SYM, Alt, right Shift, Shift+Space, Alt+Space) and the volume keys are sent for you
Gaming mode: in the Xbox player, L is the B button again rather than Android's Back

Android desktop: its desktop windowing switches, which also changed the phone's own screen (breaking Recents after a restart), are put back when the desktop ends; ones left on by earlier versions are cleared once. Restart the phone afterwards
Streaming: Moonlight's Wake is listened for on the ports Moonlight sends it to, and its broadcast is let through to the phone while a Moonlight client is paired
Gaming mode: in Dolphin, PPSSPP and the Xbox player, W A Z D (and the right stick's keys) always move the stick through the keys they were given, even where on-screen sticks were placed before
Gaming mode: a Dolphin Wii game set to a GameCube controller turns its Wii Remote off for that game in every way Dolphin reads it
Crash log: the screen and window settings section no longer shows "Failed transaction" errors
Automatic Shift: the capital after a full stop no longer goes missing when an app is slow to show the space after it
Gaming mode: in Dolphin and PPSSPP, Swap A/B and X/Y is written into the emulator's own controller settings, so the face keys reach it as they are and work again

Gaming mode: in Dolphin, every control works: Dolphin only reads the keyboard itself, so the whole layout (SYM, Shift and Alt combinations, the volume triggers, changed keys and the A/B swap) is written into its controls and every key goes to it as it is
Gaming mode: in Dolphin the volume keys are the triggers again and no longer change the volume: they're read from the phone's side buttons, a device of their own
Gaming mode: a modifier pressed just before a key is always read with it, and the keyboard's typing stays out of the way of every key in a game
Xbox Cloud Gaming: the player no longer closes straight away on Android 10, and Back goes back in the page on newer Android too
Brightness shortcuts no longer freeze the screen or typing for a moment, and screen sizes or battery saver tapped twice in a row always end on the last one tapped
Gaming mode: Recents opens again after a game changed the screen's size or turning, with another home app such as Niagara

Dolphin: a game's own controller settings are tidier: its old profiles are taken away when its controller or keys change, nothing is rewritten when unchanged (quicker starts), and its profiles follow layout changes even when Dolphin is opened on its own

Dolphin: no more "No profiles found for game setting" as a game starts: each game's own profile is named for its controller (GameCube or Wii Remote), and settings left by a controller chosen before are taken away
Gaming mode: going from a game to the Games app or Flux Keyboard's settings ends gaming mode there, and it starts again when you go back to the game
Games: the phone's Back keeps a game's changed settings, as the back arrow does (keys changed for Dolphin were lost before)

Gaming mode: Dolphin games always name Flux Keyboard's controls in their Dolphin settings, written again each time Dolphin opens, so a game started from Dolphin's own list no longer keeps a profile loaded by hand (unless the game is set to keep it)

Gaming mode: a Dolphin game's ID is read from its disc again when it was only guessed from its name before (a European Mario Kart Wii was taken for the US one, so its settings went to the wrong game); a guess now takes the region in the file's name, and a game in the list twice no longer has its two entries take turns writing its settings
Stream to Moonlight: Flux Keyboard is kept on the network while the phone sleeps (Android's battery saving cut it off), so Moonlight's Wake can reach it

Stream to Moonlight: the phone starts answering again by itself when its Wi-Fi comes back or its address changes, when streaming is turned off with Always available on, and when Moonlight's Wake arrives, so it no longer shows offline until streaming is turned off and on

Gaming mode: a Play Store game, set up as a game or as an app, has W A Z D drag its on-screen stick (low on the left unless placed with Place keys on screen): without root, a controller's stick from the keyboard is ignored by games such as Infinity Nikki; the finger slides out from the stick's centre and keeps moving a hair while held, as joysticks that follow a finger (Unreal's) need

Stream to Moonlight: streaming left on comes back on by itself after Flux Keyboard restarts (an update, the phone turned off), and Always available answers again then too; before, Moonlight saw the phone as offline until streaming was turned off and on

Gaming mode: GameHub Lite starts a Steam game straight away instead of stopping at its page (its ID sent as both its Steam and its local game ID, as ES-DE does), and GameHub Lite built under a benchmark app's name is found too
Gaming mode: a game started from Games has its screen made before its app opens, so a launcher resized as it opens a game (GameHub Lite, which closes and loses the game) no longer is

Games: a game uninstalled (its app, or its file or export taken out of the game folders) leaves the Games app, Moonlight's list and the quick launcher; one never set up is taken off, one set up is kept with its settings (marked in gaming mode's settings) for if it comes back; its home screen shortcut is turned off meanwhile

Gaming mode: after a stream ends, the key sender is started again straight away and when the next game opens, so a game opened after streaming (Infinity Nikki) gets its keys again; the crash log notes the first key in each game, when a game's text field has the keys, and which accessibility services are on
Games: a game opened from the Games app, a home screen shortcut or the quick launcher starts once, not three times while the screen changes size (GameHub Lite could close before the game loaded)

introSince: What's new in Flux Keyboard since the version you had.
